name: Magdalena Bay
label: Mom + Pop
lede: Two Miami prog-rock kids swapped Rush for Grimes, taught themselves pop off YouTube, and ended up with a concept album about a girl whose body rejects a CD.

eras.title: Prog kids in Miami
eras.text: Mica Tenenbaum and Matthew Lewin meet as teenagers in a North Miami music program and make progressive rock together. A winter break in 2016 turns them toward pop, a genre both had avoided.

q: We've been influencing each other's music taste since we were 15 years old.
years.src: Miami New Times · Gorilla vs. Bear · PAPER · Wikipedia: Magdalena Bay
years.h: Mica Tenenbaum and Matthew Lewin land in the same classic rock cover band
years.p: Both are in high school, enrolled in an after-school program at the Live! Modern School of Music in North Miami. They stay a duo for the next fifteen years.
years.xp:
The cover band did not last, but the pairing did: they formed the prog band Tabula Rasa with other musicians, including drummer [[Nick Villa|dbedcb83-60c1-4daa-9c4e-1b232b082866]], and made a self-titled EP, a self-titled album and a last record called Crimson. Tenenbaum told Gorilla vs. Bear the project was "pretty niche like progressive rock," with an audience mostly in Scandinavia.

Lewin told PAPER the pair have been swapping taste since they were teenagers, which is how a prog band ends up writing synth-pop.

years.src: Miami New Times · Gorilla vs. Bear · Wikipedia: Magdalena Bay (duo)
years.h: Winter break turns two prog kids into a pop duo
years.p: Tenenbaum is at Penn and Lewin at Northeastern, so they write by file transfer, trading Grimes and Carly Rae Jepsen records. The name comes from Maggie Bay, an administrator at Lewin's old job.
years.xp: Their first single, "Voc Pop," came out June 1, 2016 and has since been pulled from streaming. A cover of Tears for Fears' "Head over Heels" followed in September, shot on an old VHS camcorder: Tenenbaum told Miami New Times it was the first time they did the whole '80s retro thing, helped along by Miami's palm trees and neon.

eras.title: Los Angeles and a YouTube habit
eras.text: After moving to Los Angeles in 2018 the duo start releasing short videos and singles on a steady drip, and a small label bites. By 2020 they have an EP and a look: lo-fi VHS, pastel CGI.

years.src: Miami New Times · PAPER · Wikipedia: Magdalena Bay (duo)
years.h: "Afternoon in Heaven" starts Mag Minis, and a label notices
years.p: The series of home-made videos begins in February 2019. The clips are what get the pair signed to Luminelle Recordings.
years.xp:
Lewin told Miami New Times the idea behind the mini-videos was to keep a steady flow of content after the move to Los Angeles in 2018. The pair edit the videos and do the visual effects themselves, a habit that runs through every later release.

The first batch was compiled as Mini Mix Vol. 1 on July 19, 2019. Day/Pop and Night/Pop, collecting remastered singles and covers, had come out the month before the series began.

years.src: Miami New Times · Wikipedia: Magdalena Bay (duo)
yt: How to Get Physical (official video, Jan 2020)
years.h: A Little Rhythm and a Wicked Feeling, eight tracks on Luminelle
years.p: The first proper EP, released March 13, 2020.

eras.title: Mercurial World
eras.text: A debut album with its own website and video game turns into a fancam hit and a run supporting the biggest names in alt-pop. By 2023 they are at Coachella.

years.cap: Mica Tenenbaum and Matthew Lewin, October 2021
years.src: Wikipedia: Mercurial World · Gorilla vs. Bear · Wikipedia: Magdalena Bay (duo)
years.h: Mercurial World arrives with a Y2K website and an 8-bit game
years.p: Two years of home recording, out October 8, 2021 on Luminelle. Pitchfork gave it 8.0; Metacritic averaged 78.
years.xp:
The singles came in order: "Chaeri" June 30, "Secrets (Your Fire)" August 11, "You Lose!" September 15 and "Hysterical Us" October 5. Tenenbaum designed the Y2K-style promo website, and "You Lose!" got an 8-bit video game to go with its video.

"We just like making it as immersive as possible for however many people want to get lost in the sauce," Tenenbaum told Gorilla vs. Bear.

years.p: The Mercurial World track spreads in 2021 after people start using it as the soundtrack for fancam edits, according to Wikipedia.

years.cap: Live at Union Transfer, Philadelphia, November 13, 2022
years.src: Wikipedia: Mercurial World · Wikipedia: Magdalena Bay (duo)
years.h: Charli XCX brings them out on her Crash tour
years.p: Primavera Sound follows in June, and Porter Robinson's Second Sky festival in October. Drummer [[Nick Villa|dbedcb83-60c1-4daa-9c4e-1b232b082866]] joins the live lineup for good.
years.xp:
A deluxe Mercurial World followed September 23, 2022: 28 tracks, remixes by Danny L Harle and Cecile Believe, and fan-recorded voicemails dubbed "secrets."

Nick Villa, who had drummed on the album sessions since 2021, became a permanent live member that year. Tenenbaum and Lewin had known him since Tabula Rasa.

years.cap: Tenenbaum and Lewin on stage, January 5, 2023
years.h: Coachella first, Lollapalooza four months later
years.p: In between, they open for [[Caroline Polachek|d8f43dc5-4613-48ac-8c23-a62b82f8c67a]] on her Spiraling Tour and [[Rina Sawayama|52494f9b-789d-4467-bcaf-9915e70cc8f6]] on Hold the Girl Reloaded.

eras.title: The Imaginal Disk year
eras.text: Signed to Mom + Pop, the duo spend two years writing a loose sci-fi concept record, and Pitchfork ranks it among the year's best.

years.src: Wikipedia: Death & Romance · Wikipedia: Imaginal Disk
years.h: Mom + Pop gets a five-minute lead single, "Death & Romance"
years.p: Written in a two-week burst, it is the first release under the new deal. Amanda Kramer directs the sci-fi video, with Tenenbaum as True, and it opens the world of the album.
years.xp:
The track came out May 28, 2024; the video, about three minutes longer than the song, followed June 18 and ends by teasing "Fear, Sex," the next track on the record. It was the first song written for the album. [[Dave Fridmann|6b09687f-72de-4337-9a0b-da8f6248ce7c]] mixed it.

Paste later named it the best song of 2024, and it landed on Dork (#16), Stereogum (#32) and Pitchfork (#45) year-end lists.

years.big: "I was thinking a lot about psychoanalysis and reading Solaris."
years.h: True gets a disk meant to build her ideal self, and her body rejects it
years.p: Tenenbaum on where the album's concept came from, while the band was touring.
years.xp: The title borrows from the imaginal discs in insect larvae that grow into adult body parts. The cover, made with artist Maria Shatalova, shows a demon hand pushing a CD into Tenenbaum's forehead. Lewin told PAPER they leave the lyrics open-ended so listeners can put their own meaning on them.

years.cap: Live on the Imaginal Disk tour, September 24, 2024
years.src: Album of the Year · Wikipedia: Imaginal Disk
years.h: Pitchfork gives Imaginal Disk a 7.7 and ranks it No. 19 of 2024
years.p: Anna Gaca's review called it "musically and conceptually dense" for bending pop's optimism toward a more paranoid world. Metacritic averaged 85.
years.xp:
The singles were "Death & Romance" (May 28), "Image" (July 10), "Tunnel Vision" (July 31) and "That's My Floor" (August 21), all with Kramer videos. Drums were cut at the Honeymoon Suite in Los Angeles and orchestral parts in Stockholm; Justin Raisen added production on "Love Is Everywhere."

Outside Pitchfork's No. 19, NME and Stereogum both put the record at No. 5 for 2024, and Slant had it at No. 10. The Guardian and NME reviews each scored it full marks on Album of the Year's scale.

years.h: "Image" makes its late-night debut on Jimmy Kimmel Live!
years.p: The duo play it October 30, the day after a remix of the song by [[Grimes|7e5a2a59-6d9f-4a17-b7c2-e1eedb7bd222]] comes out.

eras.title: Second sleep
eras.text: The Imaginal Disk cycle runs into opening slots on the biggest tours in pop, a run of double singles, then a film.

yt: Ashes to Ashes (triple j Like A Version)
years.h: Bowie's "Ashes to Ashes" gets a sparkly cover on Triple J
years.p: The duo play it for Australia's Like a Version series on March 28, then follow it with "Image."

years.h: Billie Eilish and Halsey take them out as openers
years.p: They support [[Billie Eilish|f4abc0b5-3f7a-4eff-8f78-ac078dbce533]] on the Hit Me Hard and Soft tour and [[Halsey|3377f3bb-60fc-4403-aea9-7e800612e060]] on For My Last Trick, and play Lollapalooza on July 31.

years.h: Four double singles pile up into a box set, Nice Day
years.p: "Second Sleep" and "Star Eyes" lead off in September, with more pairs in October and November, collected as Nice Day: A Collection of Singles. Wikipedia calls the run a spiritual successor to Imaginal Disk.

years.h: Tribeca Festival gives the film its premiere
years.p: The visual album movie, announced August 23, 2025, debuts June 4. A public release has not been announced.
